sentence: A 3.5-million-year decadal-to-centennial-resolved lake sediment sequence from the monsoonal Tibetan Plateau reveals a stepped evolution of MCV that differs in detail from that of North Atlantic records.

A 3.5-million-year decadal-to-centennial-resolved lake sediment sequence from the monsoonal Tibetan Plateau reveals a stepped evolution of MCV that differs in detail from that of North Atlantic records.
From ~ 2.7 Ma, MCV became a permanent feature of glacial periods, intensifying after ~ 1.5 Ma and extending over both glacial and interglacial periods.

The embedded astronomical frequencies of MCV and their persistent linkage with precession indicate a tropical insolation origin, driven by changes in the latitudinal temperature gradient and propagated to the Tibetan Plateau via monsoonal circulation.

These findings highlight that both tropical forcing and high-latitude ice-dynamic mechanisms should be considered as “dual engines” of MCV.

Origin and dynamics of millennial climate variability Internal climate processes, such as the high-latitude Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) 45 , ice-related freshwater fluxes 46 and sea ice 47 , orbitally induced insolation changes 48 , 49 and atmospheric CO 2 50 , have been proposed to explain the origin of MCV in the climate system.

In terms of orbital forcing, the double maximum and the maximum seasonal contrast of daily irradiation received in tropical latitudes over the course of the year can generate ~11-ka, ~5.5-ka, and ~2.5-ka cycles in equatorial insolation 48 .
The changes in suborbital-millennial signals of tropical insolation (MTI) may play an active role in the response of the climate system to astronomical forcing 48 .

However, multiple proxy indicators and the specific geological context of the coring site support that the high Carb% measured in the Zoige core primarily reflect wetter climatic conditions in the region, rather than the opposite.
Lake level in this high-altitude setting is controlled by the balance between precipitation and temperature-dependent evaporation but closely tracks precipitation 73 .

Specifically, in the Zoige region, evaporation is relatively low due to cool temperatures and sufficient precipitation (mean annual temperature ~1.4 °C, summer ~10 °C; annual precipitation ~650-700 mm, falling mostly in summer).
Therefore, high Carb% measured in Zoige core are primarily related to high summer precipitation.
